title: Sparse indexer in Triton: each query token's score over the compressed keys it may see (index heads' weighted ReLU of their query-key products, on the tensor cores), then the positions of its top k keys, by radix select

scores.what: a tile of TM tokens times their index heads (TM x H rows) over a block of BN keys: the products on the tensor cores, ReLU, each head's factor and the sum over the heads in FP32 as an explicit tree (heads 2 i and 2 i + 1, then the pairs' sums: the same order whatever the tile), -inf past a token's end

TM.what: tokens a program (TM x heads tile rows, at most 128; no more than the call's tokens)

yardstick.library: torch: the products as one batched matmul (cuBLAS), then ReLU, the head weights and the head sum as tensor ops

topk.what: one token's k best scores among its valid keys by radix select (four 8-bit passes of digit histograms, then one pass writing the positions in ascending order, ties to the lower position); calls of few tokens in a CUDA kernel that holds a slice's scores in shared memory for the five passes (cuda_select.cu), the same picks

BLOCK.what: scores a step of each pass

SLICE.what: positions a program selects among before a second pass over the slices' picks (0: the rule, max(4,096, 4 k) where the tokens leave most multiprocessors idle; speed only, the same picks)

CUDA.what: 1: calls of few tokens (fewer than half the multiprocessors) select in the CUDA kernel (cuda_select.cu), a slice's scores held in shared memory for the five passes; 0: every call in the Triton programs. The same picks

yardstick.library: torch.topk over the masked scores (sorted), then the positions sorted ascending
